## Clarke's Commentary on the Bible

**Digital source.** [HelloAO Bible API](https://bible.helloao.org/api/c/adam-clarke).

**Reuse.** Public domain.

Adam Clarke's commentary was supplied by [HelloAO / AO Lab](https://bible.helloao.org/api/c/adam-clarke/books.json), which marks it [Public Domain](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/).

The provider metadata identifies the text with [Public Domain Mark 1.0](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). API software licensing is separate from the commentary text.

**Notes about this copy.** Contains commentary on 57 Bible books. Deuteronomy, Judges, Psalms, Proverbs, Ecclesiastes, Jeremiah, Joel, Malachi, and Matthew are absent. It follows the digital source, including two entries for 2 Samuel 14:27 and the reading `hath not God` at 2 John 1:9.

Adam Clarke Bible Commentary; digital text supplied by [HelloAO / AO Lab](https://bible.helloao.org/api/c/adam-clarke/books.json).

57 books and 854 chapters, with 13,318 commentary occurrences. Deuteronomy, Judges, Psalms, Proverbs, Ecclesiastes, Jeremiah, Joel, Malachi and Matthew are absent.

It preserves 4,143,242 literal characters, including 16 nonempty whitespace-only slots; there are no true-empty source strings. No missing verse is guessed or filled.

The repository README confirms the ASV provider label. The structured text and source are unchanged.

Maintained data attribution: `data/bible/asv/README.md`.

ASV electronic text supplied by [scrollmapper/bible_databases](https://github.com/scrollmapper/bible_databases).

The complete 66-book ASV JSON digital text; no complete physical 1901 edition claim.

## Berean Standard Bible

**Digital source.** [scrollmapper/bible_databases](https://github.com/scrollmapper/bible_databases).

**Credits.** Text provider: scrollmapper/bible_databases. The acquired literal marker is **BSB: Berean Standard Bible**. All 66 ordered books, 1,189 chapters and 31,102 source verse records are included, with 16 true-empty strings as empty verse slots. All literal leading/trailing spaces, wording, Unicode, numeric labels, IDs and order are conserved. Empty strings are not guessed, filled, omitted or interpreted as new editorial decisions. Only generated routing labels and explicit whitespace-preservation scaffolds are renewed.

The acquired JSON does not name translators, editors, publisher, print edition/date or rights holders. Separate openbible-io/bsb metadata associates Berean Standard Bible with **CC0-1.0** and names **BSB Publishing**. It lists **Gary Hill, Grant R. Osborne, Eugene H. Merrill, Maury Robertson, Ulrik Sandborg-Petersen and Baruch Korman** as **Advisor**, and **Gleason Archer** for **Extended translation notes**. These are precisely attributed observations of that separate metadata, not newly verified allocations to this JSON copy. Its preface names the Berean Bible Translation Committee and describes freely shareable resources. No individual role or print equivalence is inferred. The old local 2020/April 2023 claims remain historical support rather than newly confirmed source dates.

BSB electronic text supplied by [scrollmapper/bible_databases](https://github.com/scrollmapper/bible_databases). Berean Standard Bible is produced with Bible Hub, Discovery Bible, OpenBible.com and the Berean Bible Translation Committee.

**Reuse.** Public-domain dedication (CC0 1.0).

The full CC0 legal text below belongs to the separate openbible-io BSB repository; its metadata explicitly declares that license. The separately scrollmapper MIT software notice follows. Neither is silently expanded into a verified rights decision for every transformation or a claim that the spreadsheet and JSON are identical.

The provider's translation-specific README declares CC0. [The Berean Bible publisher](https://berean.bible/licensing.htm) confirms the text's public-domain dedication. CC0 terms are available at https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/. Repository software terms remain separate.

**Digital source.** [Patristic Text Archive (PTA)](https://github.com/PatristicTextArchive/pta_data).

*Ecclesiastical History* is attributed to John of Ephesus. This item contains only the surviving Syriac Part III. Parts I–II and the English Part III are not represented. The source describes its digital critical edition as preliminary and says it will be updated while the project's English translation and commentary are developed.

The source credits Nikolai Kiel as editor and Simon Birol, Philip Michael Forness, Silvio Roggo, and Hartmut Leppin as contributors. Their listed institutions include Goethe University Frankfurt and KU Leuven. The German Research Foundation (DFG) funded the project. The Berlin-Brandenburgische Akademie der Wissenschaften is the source authority; the Patristic Text Archive (PTA) distributes the 2023 edition.
